name: spec
description: Spec pipeline v7 — a small code program run by a trusted engineer, verified by executed evidence. Lifecycle: /spec:genesis (greenfield) → roadmap briefs → /spec:sketch → /spec:plan → /spec:run (design when due, then build, then review, each driver-stepped with one fresh-context reviewer and a derived verdict) → /spec:release; plus /spec:status, /spec:doctor, /spec:enforce, /spec:escape, /spec:replay. Changelog (last 3): 7.196.0 — Mock CLI spawns survive an empty inherited PATH under a version-managed node: the fallback path now leads with the directory of the node already running the driver, so the reviewer bin's `#!/usr/bin/env node` shebang resolves instead of reading as an uninstalled package. The mock journeys template gains the optional `Step.state`, `Journey.persona` and `Edge.say` fields the reviewer page reads. Core doctrine's Runtime Verification adds 'a stub is not its dependency': a leg that passed only against a stub for an out-of-scope dependency is reported unverified until re-run for real. 7.195.0 — Two drivers that used to no-op silently now refuse with a remedy. A mocks seed.md declaring no journeys left the SCREENS derivation iterating an empty set, so a mock could walk to APPROVED with no screen ever drawn; `--mark seed-done` now refuses that seed naming the `### <journey>` grammar to add. And the genesis driver's derived mock-app picks (framework, language, package-manager) were dropped without a word when brief.md carried no `## Picks` heading, leaving those dimensions recorded as neither open nor decided; MENUS now dies naming the missing heading and the picks that had nowhere to land. 7.194.0 — Corrects two stale prose claims: the sketch command no longer says the session ratifies a surface approval (only the approval made on the mock page advances it), and the roadmap-overview template no longer claims the mock viewer composes the journey graph from roadmap surfaces blocks (SEED parses those blocks into the mock app journeys.ts).
